lines.en: Hannah, this is the band that I’ve loved for years!

lines.en: Really? I’ve heard the songs that they play on the radio.
lines.pt: Sério? Já ouvi as músicas que eles tocam no rádio.

lines.en: They’re the only band that has made an album every year.

lines.en: It’s the big one that you can see from the door.
lines.pt: É o grande que dá para ver da porta.

lines.en: I’ve never been in a crowd that sings so loud!
lines.pt: Nunca estive numa multidão que canta tão alto!

lines.en: Wait until you hear the lyrics that everybody knows by heart.
lines.pt: Espere até ouvir as letras que todo mundo sabe de cor.

facts.big: A band that I’ve loved for years
facts.label: Relativa + present perfect
facts.sub: Use that ou who com o present perfect: a band that I’ve loved, a man who has sung.

facts.label: que eu já…
facts.sub: Use that + I’ve + particípio: a band that I’ve loved, the songs that I’ve heard. O objeto vem antes do that, então não repita it ou them.

facts.label: que já…
facts.sub: Use who + has/have + particípio para pessoas: the man who has sung with them, the drummer who has just joined. Who fica no lugar do sujeito.

compare.ask: It’s the band that I’ve loved for years.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “a banda que eu amo há anos”.
compare.tip: Diga: “It’s the band that I’ve loved for years.”
compare.us: Em inglês, use that para coisas e who para pessoas, seguido do present perfect: the band that I’ve loved, the man who has sung. Não repita o objeto: “the song that I’ve heard”, não “the song that I’ve heard it”.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.

extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: A concert in Glasgow · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Friday night in Glasgow. Luisa and Hal stand outside a big hall. Hal is a fan of the band. The band is on tour this month. Many people wait in a long line. Luisa has never seen them live.

“Luisa, this is the band that I’ve loved for years!” says Hal. “Really? I’ve heard the songs that they play on the radio.” says Luisa. “They’re the only band that has made an album every year.” says Hal.

pages.title: A concert in Glasgow · 3/3
paragraphs: “I’ve never been in a crowd that sings so loud!” says Luisa. “Wait until you hear the lyrics that everybody knows by heart.” says Hal. The lights go down and the crowd cheers.
